sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Color themes for light and dark
sections.what: Sets the main colors for the app in normal mode and in dark mode, such as background, text, primary and border colors. These values decide how the whole app looks in each mode.
sections.why: Defining colors once lets every component reuse the same palette.
sections.watch_out: The comment about high contrast overrides is misleading, because this block only sets colors and a base font size.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Base text, focus and motion rules
sections.what: Sets the default body text color and font size, turns on smoother text rendering, adds a visible focus ring for keyboard users, and turns off most animation for people who prefer reduced motion. It also defines a utility for text that only screen readers should read.
sections.why: These rules make the app easier to use with a keyboard and gentler for people sensitive to motion.
sections.watch_out: The focus rule removes the default outline, so any color name it uses that is missing from the setup will leave keyboard users with no visible focus.

sections.name: ::-webkit-scrollbar
sections.title: Scrollbar width
sections.what: Makes the vertical scrollbar a thin 8 pixel wide bar across the app.
sections.why: Gives a consistent, slim scrollbar that fits the healthcare look.

sections.name: ::-webkit-scrollbar-track
sections.title: Scrollbar track color
sections.what: Sets the background behind the scrollbar to the app's main background color.
sections.why: Keeps the scrollbar track blending into the page.

sections.name: ::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb
sections.title: Scrollbar handle shape and color
sections.what: Draws the draggable part of the scrollbar as a rounded, muted-color handle with a thin border.
sections.why: Makes the handle easy to see without drawing attention away from the content.

sections.name: ::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb:hover
sections.title: Scrollbar handle hover color
sections.what: Darkens the scrollbar handle slightly when the mouse moves over it.
sections.why: Gives visual feedback that the handle can be dragged.

summary: The global stylesheet that sets the app's color scheme, text size, focus outlines, motion settings and scrollbar look.
purpose: Defines the light and dark color themes used throughout the app and a few base behaviors that apply everywhere.
why: Keeping colors and base styles in one place lets the whole app change look from a single file.
how: First it sets the color values for normal mode and dark mode. Then it sets base styles for the page body, focus outlines, and motion for users who prefer less animation. It also adds a utility for hiding text from screens while keeping it for screen readers, and finally it styles the scrollbar.
inputs: Settings read from the app's Tailwind setup and from the browser (for example the reduced motion preference).
outputs: Colors, fonts, focus rings, animations and scrollbars shown across every page.
risks: The file's comment claims high contrast accessibility overrides, but it only sets a base font size, so high contrast is not actually provided. A focus style that uses a color name not in the color setup would silently do nothing.
debug: If colors look wrong, check the color values in the root and dark blocks. If focus outlines are missing, check the focus-visible rule and whether the ring color names exist in the Tailwind config.
